# ML Tuner, Frequency Shift and Multiband Delay

ML Frequency Shift adapts the complex Hilbert IIR implementation and coefficients from Signalsmith Audio's hilbert-iir header, staged in Xynth Audio FrequencyShifter revision f6bff3752cbf1420b55f7e6797effc01ac2a6e55 (https://github.com/XynthAudio/FrequencyShifter). The header is Copyright 2024 Geraint Luff / Signalsmith Audio Ltd., BSD Zero Clause; the surrounding upstream project is Copyright 2024 Xynth Audio, MIT. Both complete licences are retained alongside this document and in THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt. The Rust adaptation uses f64 complex states, two analytic filters, a continuous phase oscillator and smoothed controls. No JUCE shell is embedded. Opposite stereo shifts are supported. Zero wet shift still passes through the analytic filters; Mix 0% is exact dry at unity output. Negative-frequency and out-of-band content is attenuated. This is frequency translation, not musical transposition.

ML Tuner is a native monophonic normalized-difference (YIN) estimator with multi-period interpolation. x42 tuna.lv2 revision d6d2341e4a0b5eb71b12943e8692e14dcf0645b1 (GPL-2.0-or-later) and the existing SnapTune detector were reviewed; their source was not incorporated. A native estimator avoids a second LV2/FFTW or C++ runtime. Audio sends filtered/downsampled samples through a bounded SPSC atomic queue. A background worker estimates 27.5-2000 Hz at approximately 25 Hz; results expire after 500 ms, and reset/input changes invalidate them. Overflow resets analysis. Worker-owned buffers and bounded atomic communication keep estimation, allocation, locking and worker destruction off the audio callback. A4 calibration changes the note reference, not audio. The unmuted stereo signal is unchanged; tuning mute fades over 10 ms. This is not a polyphonic or pitch-correction tool.

ML Multiband Delay reuses the existing native ML Split phase-aligned LR4 crossover (ChowDSP topology attribution in plugins/ml-mix-core/UPSTREAM.md) and os-engine Delay's cubic Ring primitive. Six compact delay lines provide stereo low/mid/high delays up to four seconds. Time/tempo changes crossfade taps over 20 ms; gain, crossover and feedback controls are smoothed. Feedback is bounded to 90%, includes DC rejection and an extreme-level safety clamp. Sync uses host tempo with 120 BPM fallback; free mode uses milliseconds. No external multi-output routing or plugin dependencies are required. Crossover summing is magnitude-flat with allpass phase rotation. Dry at Mix 0% is exact at unity output.

All three use the shared ML editor, host parameter/state handling and Advanced DSP controls visibility. All report zero fixed audio latency; tuner analysis lag does not delay the signal. Source tests cover synthetic audio at 8-192 kHz, state/reload through the real CLAP host, tempo, bounded feedback, callback allocation/free detection and scaled editor rendering. Hands-on audio/UI and native macOS/Linux validation remain separate checks.
